facts.locator: Page 3, unified buffer and accumulator descriptions

sources.title: Jouppi et al.: In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit
Google: An in-depth look at the first TPU

limits: A historical, well-documented inference accelerator; not the latest TPU generation.
The visible array is representative, not a physical die reproduction or a drawing of every MAC.
TPU v1 stores weights in its matrix array. Doke’s separate 4 × 4 output-stationary model moves both operands and stores each output sum at a cell.
Model ticks, integer operands and memory rules are educational assumptions, not TPU instruction or performance emulation.

timing.label: 700 MHz documented clock
timing.scope: The 2017 paper’s first-generation inference TPU. Its clock period is a hardware reference; doke’s 4 × 4 output-stationary model is not this 256 × 256 weight-stationary implementation and its ticks are not TPU cycles.

limits: Cisco’s NPU terminology means Network Processing Unit. This chip moves network traffic; it is not a transformer tensor-compute engine.
The packet scene is a generic input-queued switch with authored capacity, rotating grants and model ticks. It does not emulate G200 or a proprietary Cisco scheduler.
The QoS reference documents VOQ mechanisms on named Catalyst platforms. Their Q200 SMS/HBM capacities are not attributed to G200.
The G200 data sheet used here does not disclose an exact buffer capacity, internal stage timing or a physical floorplan.

timing.label: 51.2 Tbps, full-duplex
timing.scope: Cisco’s published aggregate switching bandwidth, preserving its full-duplex convention. Not a processor clock, packet latency or guarantee of application throughput; no conversion to clock period or model ticks is made.
